title: First bands, first lawn-party job, and sitting in with Chris Kelly
summary: A band with Lawrence Randall was too timid to play; he formed one with Lawrence Toker, played a lawn party for two and a half dollars, then sat in with Chris Kelly and got hired.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: After you studied, say a couple of years, when did you start playing any jobs with the real band, not necessarily professional, or that is to get paid for, but when did you join any small group or brass band? Can you remember what you'd say is your first job or your first orchestra?

Well, after I got the drum, as I told you, my uncle got the drum from a forum shop. I was going to Lansing. I had a fellow come to bring society notice to my house. His name was Lawrence Randall. He said, I told him I had a drum. He said, well, I got a trumpet. I'm learning how to play music. He said, I'm thinking about going to Old Man Chalini. And I told him it was a good idea to go over there. And so he said, of course, I've been getting a little lessons from my uncle, Joe Nicholas. I said, yeah? I said, yeah. He said, what you say we make up a little band? I said, it's a good idea. I'd love it. So we formed a little band. Lawrence Randall, John Ankle, Gilbert, a fellow called Bush on banjo. So we would rehearse them twice a week. But the guys didn't have nerve enough to play. I felt to myself that I was about the strongest in the band. And I wasn't afraid to play, but they was. So a fellow told me about a job for Carnival. So I asked them, they told me, they said, oh man, we don't play good enough to go play no job. I said, we can make it. They said, no. So I had to give the job to somebody else and I didn't play either. So I met Lawrence Toker and he said, what you say if we make up a band? Well, he had nerve. He was Ambrose, the trombone player's nephew. So we made up a band with Lawrence Toker, Melvin Frank, Bill Hamilton. He was a banjo player. We made up a little band and we began to play together, or rehearsing, not playing a job. And a fellow named Harmon, he said that he had a house party. At that time they used to give a lot of house parties and lawn parties with short combination, like three pieces, some four pieces. He was a piano player. So you got Lawrence to play trumpet, me to play a drum. This was my first job of playing this lawn party. And we played together. The lady's name is Fenella. She have a son. He was a drummer Lionel, Torragander. I don't know if you heard of him. I've heard that name. Yeah, well, he got sick and he quit playing. But we played the job for her. And my first job was two and a half a man. A piece for each one of us. That was the job we played. So the following week, she decided to get Chris Kelly's band to play. So, well I was very interested in music. Anywhere I heard a band playing, I want to be there to learn as much as I could about playing. So on my way to the party, I meet Chris Kelly and Faisal going over to play. So he asked me to help carry his drum and that was just to my hand because I was very crazy about playing drum. So I told him on the way there, I said, I'm learning how to play drum myself. He said, yes, well that's all right. We get to the party, he plays about six or seven numbers. And he didn't say like this, say now, do you want to sit in? They used the phrase of, how's about resting me up? Let me see cuz, what you can do? Yeah. Well, I got on the drum, I started to play and so he appealed to Chris Kelly. He said, hey, he's a good little drummer. I said, where you live at? I live around the corner on Oberst Street. He said, yeah. He said, what you doing tomorrow night? I said, well, I'm not doing anything. He said, well, I think I can put you on a little job. He took me and Peter Pappy and Georgie Boyd. He was a great clarinet player. What did Pappy play? Banjo. This job was on Iberville and Marie for some Jewmakers. But he had a job at the Corporate Hall and one at the Economy Hall. That was on a Monday night because he was so popular at that time, he got a lot of jobs. Well, the drummer, Faiso, was playing with him. He put in with some other fellas and got some other band to go another job and he took me with him.
